draft.title: Anaerobic and resistance training
card: Anaerobic training uses short, high-intensity efforts, such as sprints, with rest between them. It trains the anaerobic energy systems, which supply energy fast without needing oxygen.
Work and rest times are planned. Short, all-out efforts mainly load the ATP-PC system. Longer hard efforts of about 30 seconds to 2 minutes also load the lactic acid system.
Resistance training makes muscles work against a load, such as free weights, machines, resistance bands or body weight. Push-ups and squats are body weight exercises.
Heavier loads with fewer repetitions mainly build strength. Moving a moderate load quickly mainly builds power, which is force produced at speed.
draft.remember: Anaerobic training uses short, hard efforts with rest. Resistance training works muscles against a load to build strength and power.

a.q: Which session is an example of anaerobic interval training?
opts: Eight 100 m sprints, each followed by a long walk back
A steady 40 minute jog at a comfortable pace
A 5 km run that alternates between jogging and walking
A 60 minute swim at an even, easy pace
a.why: Short, all-out sprints with rest between them train the anaerobic systems. The jog and swim are steady and long, and the run and walk mix is a continuous aerobic session, not short hard efforts with planned rest.
a.clue: Look for short, all-out efforts with planned rest.

b.q: Jess is a netball player who wants to jump higher and push off faster. Which training best matches her goal?
opts: Squat jumps and light weights lifted quickly
A steady 10 km run at an even pace
Holding stretches for 30 seconds each
Light jogging for 60 minutes each session
b.why: Power is force produced at speed, so moving a moderate load quickly suits jumping. Steady running and long jogging build endurance, not power. Holding stretches works on range of movement, not power.
b.clue: Which choice builds force at speed?

a.best: Eight 100 m sprints, each followed by a long walk back

b.best: Squat jumps and light weights lifted quickly

problems.detail: The right option says 'light weights lifted quickly', but the card and the why say power comes from moving a 'moderate load' quickly. The option and the card should use the same load description.

The why calls the 5 km jog-walk run 'a continuous aerobic session', but alternating jogging and walking is not continuous training. It would be better to say it is low-intensity aerobic work, not short all-out efforts.
